title: Revealing the Role of Individual Metal-Support Interactions in Hydrogen Production for Heterogeneous Photocatalysts via 4DSTEM Techniques
content: Supported metal photocatalysts play a pivotal role in mediating hydrogen production in sunlight-activated molecule splitting reactions, a promising avenue for cheap green hydrogen. The efficiency of hydrogen production in such systems is determined by catalytic reactivity, selectivity, and stability which are in turn affected by the electronic interplay between metal catalyst and oxide support. These metal-support interactions (MSIs) occur due to the chemical bond formation between metal nanoparticle (NP) catalysts and supports and can result in deformation of the support lattice among other physical and chemical phenomena [1, 2]. Distinct MSIs can involve varying levels of charge transfer and physical interactions between metal NP and support, thereby serving as effective tuning parameters for optimizing catalytic performance [3]. However, individual MSIs are not static are subject to physical and chemical changes in their environment during catalytic activation. Thus the precise characterization of the atomic and electronic structure of individual MSIs is vital to understanding the dynamic nature of MSIs and its link to hydrogen production efficiency.
